name: solve-js-architecture
description: Module map, data flow, and architectural constraints for the solve-js engine
prompt:
You are working on the solve-js project. Understand the full architecture:

## Pipeline (the only thing that matters)
Source text → Lexer → Parser → BytecodeCompiler → VM → Value result → Cache

## Module Map and Responsibilities

CORE:
- lexer/ (Lexer, MarkdownLexer) — Tokenise markdown + expressions. Self-contained, no deps.
- lexer/registry/ (TokenRegistry) — Token type definitions.
- parser/ (Parser) — Pratt parsing → AST. Depends on ParseletRegistry.
- parser/ (BytecodeBuilder) — AST → bytecode. Depends on OpCode.
- parser/registry/ (ParseletRegistry) — Register prefix/infix parselets.
- parser/ (BindingPower) — Operator precedence table.
- parser/ (OpCode) — Opcode enum definitions.
- vm/ (VM) — Execute bytecode → Value. Depends on OpRegistry, Value, DependencyGraph.
- vm/ (ScopeManager) — Variable scope and resolution. Depends on VariableResolver, DependencyGraph.
- vm/ (DependencyGraph) — Track line→variable dependencies. No deps.
- vm/ (Value) — Typed immutable value representation. No deps.
- vm/ (MemoCache) — Result caching (epoch-based). No deps.
- cache/ (LineCache) — Per-line result + bytecode cache. No deps.
- cache/ (UnifiedCache, LFUCache) — Generic cache (LEGACY — deprecated).
- engine/ (ExpressionEngine) — Orchestrates full pipeline. Can import everything.
- engine/ (DynamicValueResolver) — Resolves dynamic values. Depends on ExpressionEngine.

PROVIDERS (domain logic):
- providers/arithmetic/ — Basic math operators
- providers/percentage/ — Percentage calculations
- providers/function/ — Math functions (sqrt, pow, etc.)
- providers/datetime/ — Date/time operations
- providers/uom/ — Unit of measurement conversion
- providers/vector/ — Vector operations (2D, 3D, 4D)
- providers/biginteger/ — Big integer support
- providers/dice/ — Dice roll simulation
- providers/variables/ — Variable assignment and resolution

All providers register parselets and opcodes. They MUST NOT import from engine/.

PLUGINS AND API:
- plugins/ (PluginSystem) — External plugin management
- api/ (SolveAPI) — Public API exposure
- workers/ (DataQueryWorker, DataSourceStrategy) — Web worker and data handling
- diagnostics/ (Collector, Pipeline, Events) — Diagnostic event system
- errors/ (UnifiedErrorFramework) — SolveError, Result<T,E>, ErrorFactory
- types/ (ParsingResult, core) — Shared type definitions
- format/ (FormatEngine) — Output formatting

## Architectural Rules
1. STRICT TOP-DOWN dependency direction. Nothing imports upward.
2. vm/ does NOT import parser/ or lexer/.
3. providers/ may import parser/ and vm/ types but NOT engine/.
4. cache/ is dependency-free.
5. One primary export per file, filename matches export.

## Caching Strategy
- Bytecode cache: expression string → BytecodeProgram (long-lived, invalidated on grammar change)
- Result cache: line + hash → Value (per-document, invalidated by DAG)
- DAG dirty tracking: variable → dependent lines (triggers selective re-eval)

## Why Bytecode VM?
- Bytecode is cacheable (expression → bytecode is expensive, bytecode → result is cheap)
- Enables instruction limits for safety
- Provides stable compilation target for plugins

## Why Pratt Parsing?
- Clean separation of prefix/infix operators
- Easy extension via parselet registration
- Natural precedence via binding powers
